Pericardial fluid analysis revealed reactive mesothelial cells, histiocytes, and dense mixed inflammation with numerous neutrophils but no malignant cells or granulomas. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial abdominal CT from FUO workup in patient subsequently diagnosed with FMF (FMF mimicking Whipple's disease article); caption/in-text explicitly state enteritis which maps to transient small-bowel wall thickening vocabulary term. B: Sagittal reformatted abdominal CT part of same Figure 2 showing mesenteric changes and enteritis in FMF patient; same caption attribution as panel A. C: Coronal abdominal CT part of same Figure 2 demonstrating bowel wall edema/enteritis attributed to FMF FUO episode mimicking Whipple's disease.

in_text_mentions: The patient underwent work up for fever of unknown origin (FUO) with chest and abdominal CT scan. CT scans and endoscopy of his gastrointestinal tract as work up for FUO had been carried out prior to the diagnosis of FMF and was unremarkable. This time CTs revealed paraaortic and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, hyperaemia and congestion of the mesenteric vessels, turbidity of the mesenteric fat and enteritis (Figure 2).
